articleHtml:
McAlister’s Deli meals often contain more than the item named on the menu.

A sandwich can include a side. A Giant Spud can come with butter and sour cream. A salad may need dressing counted separately. A Choose 2 combines portions from two different menu categories, while tea, cookies, chips, soup, or mac and cheese can add another part to the meal.

Use the McAlister’s Deli Nutrition Calculator above to compare individual items and build the complete order you actually eat.

Start With the Exact Sandwich

McAlister’s sandwiches use very different combinations of turkey, ham, roast beef, chicken salad, bacon, cheese, spreads, vegetables, and bread.

The McAlister’s Club, for example, combines turkey, Black Forest ham, bacon, cheddar, Swiss, vegetables, mayo, and McAlister’s Honey Mustard on wheat.

That is very different from a simpler turkey sandwich or roast beef sandwich.

When nutrition is available for the complete standard recipe, use that value first rather than trying to reconstruct the sandwich from generic deli ingredients.

Bread Choice Can Make a Noticeable Difference

McAlister’s currently allows several bread substitutions on many sandwiches.

Depending on the item and location, options can include:

Croissant

Marbled Rye

Wheat Wrap

Sliced Wheat

Baguette

Ciabatta

Country White

Jalapeño Roll

9-Grain Bread

and gluten-free bread where available.

These options do not contain the same calories or carbohydrates.

If you change the standard bread, calculate the version that matches your order rather than keeping the nutrition for the original sandwich.

Sandwich Calories May Include More Than the Sandwich

This is particularly important at McAlister’s.

Current ordering pages show many sandwiches with a required side selection. Depending on the way the restaurant publishes the headline calorie value, you need to understand whether the displayed total represents the standard sandwich alone or a particular standard configuration.

NutritionSolver should make this explicit with a short label such as:

Sandwich only

or

Includes standard side

where verified.

This prevents users from accidentally adding the same side twice.

McAlister’s Club Is a Major Menu Benchmark

The McAlister’s Club is one of the brand’s signature sandwiches.

The current official menu lists the standard McAlister’s Club at about 900 calories before further customizations are made.

Changing bread, removing mayo, replacing Honey Mustard, adding avocado, or adding another protein can alter the result.

For customized orders, calculate only the changes you actually make.

Giant Spuds Are Full Entrées, Not Small Potato Sides

McAlister’s Giant Spuds are large baked potato meals.

They can combine potato, butter, sour cream, cheese, meats, vegetables, sauces, or mac and cheese depending on the recipe.

Current options include items such as:

Spud Max

Chicken Bacon Ranch Spud

Smokehouse Spud

Honey BBQ Pork Spud

Bacon Spud

Veggie Spud

and Cheese Spud .

These should be treated as full entrées rather than as sides.

Spud Max Combines Several Toppings

The current Spud Max includes ham, turkey, bacon, cheddar-jack, green onions, and black olives, with butter and sour cream.

Its current standard nutrition is approximately 1,090 calories and 45g of protein .

Removing butter or sour cream changes the total. Adding avocado, chicken, ranch, cheese dip, or another topping changes it again.

This makes Giant Spuds particularly suitable for ingredient-level customization.

High Protein Does Not Automatically Mean Low Calorie

Several current Giant Spuds provide substantial amounts of protein.

McAlister’s currently highlights Chicken Bacon Ranch Spud, Smokehouse Spud, Honey BBQ Pork Spud, and Spud Max among its protein-focused options.

But protein is only one part of the comparison.

A loaded potato can also contain substantial amounts of carbohydrates, fat, saturated fat, and sodium.

For a useful comparison, review:

Calories

Protein

Carbohydrates

Fat

Sodium

together.

Choose 2 Needs Its Own Calculator Logic

The Choose 2 is one of the most important McAlister’s-specific features.

Instead of ordering one full entrée, you combine smaller portions from eligible menu categories.

A Choose 2 might pair:

Half sandwich + cup of soup

Half sandwich + salad

Spud portion + soup

or another supported combination.

Because the final nutrition depends on both selections, there is no useful universal calorie number for “McAlister’s Choose 2.”

The calculator should add the two exact portions selected.

Use Choose 2 Portions, Not Full Entrée Values

This serving distinction matters.

A sandwich can have:

Full sandwich nutrition

and a separate:

Choose 2 portion

The same can happen with starters or other eligible foods.

For example, a full entrée and its Choose 2 portion may differ dramatically.

NutritionSolver should clearly label these as separate serving sizes so users do not accidentally combine two full entrées while trying to calculate a Choose 2.

Soup Needs the Correct Cup or Bowl Size

McAlister’s serves soups in more than one portion.

Current options include soups such as:

Broccoli Cheddar

Chicken Tortilla

Country Potato

Traditional Chili

Veggie Chili

and seasonal or newer soups depending on location.

Where Cup and Bowl servings are available, they should always be separate entries.

A Bowl should never inherit the calories of a Cup.

Salad Dressing Can Change the Meal Significantly

McAlister’s salads contain ingredients such as chicken, cheese, bacon, nuts, dried fruit, avocado, vegetables, and croutons depending on the recipe.

Then comes the dressing.

Current dressing choices can include:

Sherry Shallot

Ranch

Caesar

Chipotle Ranch

McAlister’s Honey Mustard

Thousand Island

and vinaigrettes.

Some dressings add far more calories and fat than others.

If dressing is published separately, include the one you actually use rather than treating every salad as nutritionally complete without it.

Savannah Chopped Salad Is More Than Greens

The Savannah Chopped Salad combines grilled chicken, dried cranberries, Gorgonzola, honey-roasted almonds, tomatoes, cucumbers, and mixed greens.

That combination explains why its nutrition differs substantially from a simple Garden Salad.

The current NutritionSolver entry contains approximately 450 calories and 36g of protein before considering whether your chosen dressing is already incorporated into that specific nutrition record.

Always verify the serving definition before adding dressing.

Famous Sweet Tea Belongs in the Meal Total

McAlister’s Famous Tea is a major part of the brand.

The current beverage menu also allows customers to customize drinks with fruit purées and combinations such as flavored Sweet Tea, lemonade teas, and flavored fountain drinks.

A plain unsweetened tea and a Sweet Tea with additional fruit flavoring can have very different carbohydrate and sugar totals.

For beverage nutrition, always identify:

Drink

Size

Sweetened or unsweetened

Flavor additions

before calculating the total.

Gallons Should Never Be Confused With Individual Drinks

McAlister’s also sells Famous Tea and lemonade by the gallon.

A gallon of Famous Sweet Tea is currently listed at roughly 1,370 calories and is intended for multiple servings.

That should appear as:

McAlister’s Famous Sweet Tea, Gallon

not simply:

Sweet Tea

Otherwise, a large catering container can be confused with an individual drink.

The same rule applies to gallon lemonade and flavored gallon beverages.

Starters Often Have Sharing Portions

Nachos and other starters can have serving definitions intended for multiple people.

For example, McAlister’s may distinguish between a Choose 2 portion and a larger starter designed to serve several people.

If a starter is labeled “Serves 2-4,” the full nutrition belongs to the whole platter.

If you share it, calculate the portion you personally eat rather than assigning yourself the entire dish.

Sides Can Change a Sandwich Meal Quickly

McAlister’s sandwiches can be paired with several sides.

Current ordering options can include:

Chips

Garden Salad

Caesar Salad

Cup of Soup

Mac & Cheese

and other location-dependent sides.

These choices have very different nutrition.

For example, replacing a simple side with a Caesar salad or Mac & Cheese can change the meal by hundreds of calories.

The calculator should make the side a separate, visible decision.

Cookies and Desserts Need Their Own Entry

McAlister’s sells cookies, brownies, cheesecake, and other desserts.

If you order dessert after a sandwich, salad, soup, or Giant Spud, include it separately in the meal total.

This is especially important for box meals and catering combinations where a cookie may already be included.

Check the bundle definition before adding another dessert.

Calculate the Complete McAlister’s Meal

Start with the exact sandwich, Giant Spud, salad, soup, starter, or Choose 2 combination .

Then confirm the correct portion size, bread, toppings, dressing, side, and sauce .

Finally, add the Famous Tea, lemonade, chips, cookie, dessert, or other beverage that is actually part of your order.

That produces a much more useful McAlister’s nutrition total than looking at one entrée number by itself.

faqs.q: How does McAlister’s Choose 2 work for nutrition?
faqs.a: Choose 2 combines smaller eligible portions from two menu selections. Calculate the exact Choose 2 portions rather than adding two full entrée values.

faqs.q: Are McAlister’s soup Cup and Bowl calories different?
faqs.a: Yes. Cup and Bowl servings contain different quantities and should have separate nutrition values.
It can. Check whether the published salad nutrition includes its standard dressing. If dressing is excluded or changed, add the dressing you actually use.

faqs.q: Does changing sandwich bread change the calories?
faqs.a: Yes. McAlister’s bread choices have different calorie and carbohydrate values, so a bread substitution changes the finished sandwich.
No. Famous Sweet Tea contains sugar and calories. Unsweetened tea is a different beverage and should have its own nutrition entry.
